newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa arrests policeman on corruption charge.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa arrests policeman on corruption charge.

text.p: A South African police sergeant was arrested on Tuesday on corruption charges after being arrested in a "sting" operation, police said.

Police Superintendent Eugene Opperman said in a statement detectives acted on information received from a man who accused the sergeant of illegally seizing his car two days ago and demanding 2,500 rand ($550) to give it back.

The man also accused the same officer of helping him to avoid prosecution on a charge of robbery "some time ago". The sergeant allegedly stole case exhibits, which led to the case being withdrawn in court.
Opperman said the sergeant, stationed at the Boksburg North police station, was arrested after money changed hands in the sting operation.
The car was recovered. Opperman said it had never been officially handed in at any police station.
The sergeant was granted bail of 7,000 rand ($1,500) later on Tuesday after a court hearing, but Opperman said he was kept in custody as he had not raised the cash.
"The South African Police Service wants to warn police officers with corrupt ideas that we will deal with them severely," Opperman said, calling on the public to report similar cases.
The case was the second incident of arrests for corruption report within two days in the satellite suburbs around Johannesburg.

On Monday, Kempton Park police said they had arrested two interpreters and a court clerk over the theft of a charge sheet which they had planned to sell to the accused in the case for 5,000 rand ($1,075).
Crime is one of President Nelson Mandela government's most urgent priorities. Police figures show 5,863 murders were reported around the country from January to March this year.
